The natural cave through which  Tunnel Creek flows is a major attraction of the park.
Many Aboriginal rock paintings and speleothems are present in the cave decorating the walls. The cave was the hideout of the Aboriginal warrior Jandamarra, who was killed outside the entrance of the cave in 1897. It is part of the  Balili (Devonian Reef) Conservation Park.


== Geography ==
The park is located in the Napier Range and covers an area of 91 hectares (220 acres). The range is composed of limestone and is the remains of a Devonian reef system formed around 350 million years ago.
The tunnel component of Tunnel Creek has a length of approximately 750 m (2,460 ft) that runs underground and is one of the oldest cave systems in Western Australia. The reef was first exposed around 250 million years ago and the first cave systems began to form; the present cave systems were created about 20 million years ago.
The cave reaches a maximum height of 12 m (39 ft) and has a maximum width of 15 m (49 ft).
